data.title: New Zealand consumer confidence hits 10-month high as fuel prices fall
data.description:
New Zealand's consumer confidence rebounded in November to its highest level since January, as shoppers grew more upbeat on the back of falling fuel prices at the pump, ANZ-Roy Morgan data showed on Friday.

The consumer confidence index rose to 100.2 in November, up from 96.2 in October, as two-year inflation expectations eased to their lowest level in nearly two years. A reading above 100 indicates optimism, while a reading below 100 signals pessimism.

"Consumers (are) feeling more chipper about their future prospects than their current circumstances. Still, it was good to see both the current and future conditions indexes rise this month," the survey said.

data.title: Organto Foods Delivers Record Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
Third Quarter Sales +67% Versus PY

Third Consecutive Positive Adjusted EBITDA Quarter

Balance Sheet Remains Strong

VANCOUVER, BC AND BREDA, THE NETHERLANDS / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Organto Foods Inc. ("Organto" or "the Company"), is pleased to announce its financial results for the three and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are expressed in Canadian dollars and in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), except where specifically noted.

"Q-3 2026 was another record quarter for our Company. Our third quarter sales grew 67% to $25.2 million, the largest third quarter sales in the history of the Company, while gross profit, adjusted gross profit (1) and adjusted EBITDA (1) also reached third quarter records. Equally important, our balance sheet remains strong with $14.5 million of working capital, no long-term debt and net equity of $15.6 million. Following our business repositioning through 2024 and early 2025, our goal was to continue to expand our commercial and operating base, while positioning to achieve positive adjusted EBITDA (1) in 2026. We have realized these objectives and in fact this quarter represents our third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA (1) results, demonstrating the strength and adaptability of our scalable, capital-efficient ecosystem. These results reinforce our confidence in the opportunities that lie ahead as we continue to build a world-class organic and fairtrade foods company." commented Steve Bromley, Co-Chair and Chief Executive Officer.

Key Highlights

  • Sales increased 67% to a third quarter record of $25.2 million. Largest third quarter sales in Company's history.
  • Adjusted gross profit (1) when accounting for the impact of currency hedging related to gross profit increased to $2.1 million or 8.2% of sales, an increase of 206% versus the prior year. Largest third quarter gross profit and adjusted gross profit (1) dollars in the Company's history.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) decreased to 7.8% of sales versus 8.9% in the prior year, demonstrating continued operating leverage.
  • Adjusted EBITDA (1) improved to $0.3 million from a loss of $0.7 million in the prior year. Largest third quarter adjusted EBITDA (1) in the Company's history.
  • Annualized sales run rate (2) continues in excess of $100 million.
  • Working capital increased to $14.5 million.
  • No long-term debt outstanding.
  • Cash balance remained strong at $7.9 million.
  • Equity of $15.6 million, up 78% versus December 31, 2025

Steve Bromley further commented, "We remain focused and committed to building a world-class organic and fairtrade foods company serving growing global healthy and sustainable foods markets, with the goal of creating long-term value for our operating partners, customers, team members and shareholders. We continue to gain momentum in our business and believe our third quarter results reflect another important point in our journey. At the same time, we are working to expand our geographic footprint and product mix with the goal of increasing our market presence and operating margins through increased value-add."

Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Results Overview

  • Third quarter 2026 sales of $25.2 million versus $15.1 million in the prior year, an increase of approximately 67%. Sales increased as new business was on-boarded and existing customers increased their sales versus the prior year. Sales for the third quarter of 2026 are the largest third quarter sales in the Company's history.
  • Gross profit of $1.5 million or 5.8% of sales, versus $1.2 million or 8.2% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 18% in gross profit dollars. Adjusted gross profit (1) of $2.1 million or 8.2% of sales when accounting for the impact of realized gains on derivatives related to gross profit versus $0.7 million or 4.5% of sales in the prior year, an increase of approximately 206%. Gross profit and adjusted gross profit (1) dollars for the third quarter of 2026 are the largest third quarter gross profit dollars in the history of the Company.
  • Cash overhead expenses (1) of $2.0 million or7.8% of sales versus $1.3 million or 8.9% of sales in the prior year. Cash overhead expenses (1) as a percentage of sales improved versus the prior periods as the business continues to grow and scale and overheads are leveraged on an expanded platform.   • Income from operations (1) excluding stock-based compensation and including realized gains/losses on derivatives related to gross profit of $0.0 million versus a loss of $0.7 million in the prior year.

Unrealized loss on derivative assets of $0.5 million versus an unrealized gain of $1.0 million in the prior year. Derivative assets represent hedges on foreign currencies which are intended to protect the Company's gross profit.
  • Net loss for the third quarter of $1.4 million versus a net loss of $2.0 million in the third quarter of the prior year. Prior year results include a loss on the settlement of debt of $1.7 million and restructuring costs of $0.1 million related to the restructuring of the balance sheet which occurred in 2025.

Fiscal 2026 Nine-Month Results Overview

data.title: Final New Zealand election vote count to confirm parliament make up
data.description:
Final government election results are due to be released in New Zealand later on Friday, with the official count expected to confirm whether the incumbent centre-right government can hold on to its razor-slim majority.

Preliminary results released by New Zealand’s Electoral Commission after the November 7 election showed the incumbent three-party ruling coalition led by National had a majority of two seats, after an election dominated by a struggling economy and voter ​disillusionment with the two biggest contenders.

The final results released on Friday will include around 400,000 special votes, which include ballots cast overseas and those requiring additional checks. Those votes have typically favoured the left, with parties on the right losing support following the count. This could also ​be key in seats where races remain tight between Labour and National candidates.

Party leaders are expected to respond after the results are published, as negotiations over a possible governing arrangement gather pace.

Under New Zealand's proportional representation system, parties frequently need support agreements with smaller partners to form an administration.

There are 71 constituency seats and at least 49 party seats, and a party or coalition needs a majority to form a government.

The final tally will also settle the number of electorate and list seats won by each party, providing a clearer picture of the balance of power for the next parliamentary term.

data.title: Targinta secures patents in Europe, China and the USA for integrin α10 antibodies in aggressive cancers
data.description:
Targinta (subsidiary of Xintela) announces that the company has been granted new patents in three major markets for its integrin α10 antibody technology: a European patent for triple-negative breast cancer, a Chinese patent that also covers other aggressive cancers, and a second US patent for the diagnosis of brain tumours.

The European Patent Office has granted EP 3 956 360, which covers antibodies that bind integrin α10 and inhibit the growth of cancer cells, for the treatment of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), as well as methods for diagnosis and prognosis. The patent has unitary effect in 18 EU member states, is also in force in the United Kingdom and Switzerland, and can be maintained until April 2040.

The China National Intellectual Property Administration has granted patent ZL 202080043354.8, covering defined integrin α10 antibodies for the treatment and diagnosis of TNBC and other aggressive cancers, including lung and pancreatic cancer. This patent is also in force until April 2040.

The US Patent and Trademark Office has issued US 12,806,280, Targinta's second US patent in the patent family for tumours of the central nervous system. The patent covers methods for detecting integrin α10 in samples from the central nervous system in order to identify tumours. Covered tumour types include glioma and glioblastoma, and the patent is in force until September 2037. The patent family is also granted in Europe, Japan and several other countries.

“These patents provide our integrin α10 antibodies broader protection and strengthen our patent position in several major markets. Together with our product patent applications for TARG9 and TARG10, this gives Targinta and future partners a strong foundation for exclusivity in some of the most aggressive and difficult-to-treat cancers”, says Evy Lundgren-Åkerlund, CEO of Targinta.

About Xintela och Targinta

Xintela (XINT) is a publicly-traded clinical-stage biopharma company developing cutting edge medical products in stem cell therapy and targeted cancer therapy. Xintela’s proprietary technology uses the stem cell marker integrin α10β1 to select and quality-assure stem cells in the product XSTEM®, which has shown safety and positive efficacy in a clinical study on knee osteoarthritis and has completed a clinical study on difficult-to-heal leg ulcers. Xintela’s in-house GMP-facility manufactures XSTEM and provides process development and manufacturing of other cell therapies. Xintela’s wholly owned subsidiary Targinta AB develops First-in-Class therapeutic antibodies targeting integrin α10β1. TARG9, an Antibody-Drug Conjugate (ADC), and TARG10, a function blocking antibody, are in preclinical development for the treatment of aggressive, difficult-to-treat cancers including glioblastoma, triple-negative breast cancer and sarcoma. Xintela conducts its business at Medicon Village in Lund, Sweden, and is listed on Nasdaq First North Growth Market Stockholm. Xintela's Certified Adviser is Västra Hamnen Corporate Finance AB..

data.title: Bitcoin Miners Go 98 Minutes Without Finding a Single Block
data.description:
Bitcoin miners experienced their longest dry spell since July on Nov. 26. According to Galaxy's Alex Thorn, it took Bitcoin miners 98 minutes and 19 seconds to find the next block.

That's the third time in 2026 that miners have gone this long without finding a block. The wait ended at 18:28 UTC on Thursday.

For anyone trying to get Bitcoin transactions confirmed shortly after the previous block, the gap meant waiting more than an hour and a half.

Even if you paid a very high transaction fee, you would still have to wait until a miner found the next block before your transaction could receive its first confirmation.

Thursday's gap was the 69th longest since 2011, according to Galaxy Research. It was just three minutes shy of the threshold for the top 50.

And this year's other long gap lasted nearly two hours. On July 6, miners took 112 minutes and 26 seconds to find the next block (number 956,953). That was the 19th longest gap on record, according to Galaxy.

How can a 10-minute interval result in a 98-minute wait?

Bitcoin automatically adjusts mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to keep the average block interval at around 10 minutes.

However, blocks sometimes are found seconds apart. Other times, it takes well over an hour for the next block to be found.

At any given mining difficulty, the chance that a single attempt to find a block will succeed is incredibly small.

If miners have spent 90 minutes trying to find the next block, the chance of succeeding on the next attempt is the same as it was on the first attempt.

So the expected time until the next block is found is still 10 minutes, even if it's already been 90 minutes since the last block was found. That's assuming the network's total computing power and mining difficulty remain unchanged.

Assuming an average block interval of 10 minutes, Thorn said you could expect a gap of at least 98 minutes and 19 seconds about once every 18,600 block intervals.

That means such a gap should occur roughly once every four months, based on an average of about 144 blocks per day.

How the historical rankings can change

Galaxy examined 877,290 block intervals going back to Jan. 1, 2011.

Researchers identified 1,948 intervals where at least an hour had passed between the timestamps of successive blocks.

However, Galaxy flagged 97 of those intervals because an adjacent block had a timestamp that was off by at least 10 minutes. This raised questions about the actual length of those gaps.

The longest recorded interval is particularly interesting.

On Nov. 30, 2011, block 155,290 seemingly marked the end of a 144-minute-and-50-second gap.

However, the miner who found the next block had set its timestamp back by 65 minutes.

After excluding apparent timestamp errors, the longest gap was 141 minutes and one second, recorded on Oct. 13, 2011.

data.title: Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Plunges $6 Billion: The Cost of His Bitcoin Bet
data.description:
Key takeaways

  • Michael Saylor’s estimated net worth has fallen about $6 billion, from $9.3 billion in October 2025 to roughly $3.3 billion on November 25, 2026, a 64.5% drop per Forbes.
  • The $6 billion is a drop in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any asset sales.
  • Saylor’s personal 17,732 BTC (bought for about $175 million) would be worth roughly $1.07 billion at $60,325, assuming he still holds them all.
  • Strategy holds 851,305 BTC bought at an average $75,446, leaving a paper shortfall of about $12.88 billion against its $64.23 billion cost.
  • Strategy’s mNAV was 0.94 at the November 25 close, so raising capital by issuing shares has become harder, and that matters as much as the Bitcoin price.

Michael Saylor’s net worth has fallen by approximately $6 billion since the cryptocurrency market peaked in October 2025. The Strategy co-founder, whose fortune was estimated at $9.3 billion at the time, is now worth around $3.3 billion, according to Forbes.

The decline has wiped out nearly two-thirds of Saylor’s estimated wealth. Yet the billionaire’s company continues to accumulate Bitcoin despite mounting paper losses, showing little willingness to reconsider its investment strategy.

For Saylor, the downturn presents a problem that extends well beyond the price of Bitcoin. Much of his fortune depends on a company that must convince investors to keep financing its accumulation strategy.

How Much Has Michael Saylor Lost During the Bitcoin Crash?

Saylor was already among the cryptocurrency industry’s biggest financial casualties in February, when Forbes estimated that his wealth had fallen by $4.7 billion from its October 2025 level.

His fortune briefly stabilized in the following months, reaching an estimated $4.7 billion in June, before suffering another setback.

Bitcoin’s return to the $60,000 level has added pressure, but the cryptocurrency alone does not explain the scale of the decline. Saylor’s exposure through Strategy makes his financial position considerably more complicated than that of an ordinary Bitcoin investor.

The $6 billion represents a reduction in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any disclosed asset sales.

How Much Bitcoin Does Michael Saylor Personally Own?

In October 2020, Saylor disclosed that he personally owned 17,732 BTC, acquired for approximately $175 million.

At the Bitcoin price of $60,325 reported by Strategy on November 26, those holdings would be worth approximately $1.07 billion, assuming he still owns the entire disclosed amount.

That would leave his original personal investment with an unrealized gain of roughly $895 million.

His current personal Bitcoin balance has not been independently confirmed, but the calculation illustrates an important distinction. Saylor can lose billions in estimated wealth while remaining substantially profitable on his original Bitcoin purchases.

The situation at Strategy is quite different.

Strategy Is Sitting on Nearly $13 Billion in Bitcoin Paper Losses

While Saylor began buying Bitcoin at considerably lower prices, his company has spent much of the past several years increasing its exposure at higher valuations.

According to its November 23 SEC filing, Strategy acquired another 457 BTC for $29.6 million, bringing its total holdings to 851,305 BTC.

The company has spent approximately $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446.

Its official Bitcoin dashboard valued those reserves at approximately $51.35 billion on November 26.

That leaves a gap of nearly $12.9 billion between the company’s cumulative acquisition cost and the market value of its Bitcoin holdings.

These figures do not represent realized trading losses, nor do they capture the full financial performance of the company.

Nevertheless, the numbers reveal how dramatically the economics of accumulating Bitcoin have changed during the downturn.

Why Saylor’s Fortune Is Vulnerable to More Than Bitcoin

For years, investors were willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares. The attraction was not simply the Bitcoin it owned, but the prospect that management could raise additional capital and increase shareholders’ exposure to the cryptocurrency.

That premium is no longer something the company can take for granted.

Strategy’s dashboard showed an mNAV ratio of 0.94 at the November 25 stock market close, using its own net Bitcoin value per share methodology.

The company’s latest investor briefing acknowledges the implications:

“

A widening discount can cause MSTR to underperform BTC even when bitcoin rises.

Strategy · Investor briefing

This is where Saylor’s investment model faces a more difficult test.

When investors are willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares, raising capital to acquire more Bitcoin can improve the economics of the business. When that premium disappears, issuing additional shares becomes a more complicated proposition.

Strategy’s own sensitivity analysis shows that a Bitcoin price of $40,000 would reduce its estimated net reserve value per share to $45.37, compared with $163.17 at a Bitcoin price of $100,000. The figures illustrate how sensitive the company’s underlying reserve valuation is to Bitcoin price movements.

Strategy’s third-quarter financial results offer a clearer picture of why its cash reserves and financing obligations now matter almost as much as the price of Bitcoin.

Buying more Bitcoin is only one part of the equation. The cost of financing those purchases matters just as much.

Could Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Recover?

There is a credible case for recovery. Strategy still owns more than 850,000 Bitcoin, giving it considerable exposure to any sustained cryptocurrency market rebound.

The company also reported approximately $4.82 billion in combined cash and dollar reserves in its latest investor briefing, providing a buffer against its financing obligations.

But a recovery in Bitcoin would not necessarily produce an equivalent recovery in Saylor’s wealth. Strategy’s share price also depends on its debt, preferred-stock obligations, access to capital and the valuation investors are willing to assign to its business model.

The next test for Saylor is not whether he can buy another thousand Bitcoin. It is whether he can continue financing those purchases on terms that benefit existing shareholders.

His personal fortune has already demonstrated how expensive that distinction can become.

This allowance represents a significant milestone in the Company's ongoing commitment to innovation, product development and delivering advanced solutions to contractors worldwide. The patent is expected to be formally issued in due course.

SPACE-R addresses three challenges in creating reinforced concrete columns. First, it replaces the traditional horizontal steel stirrup with a lightweight fiberglass component, significantly reducing shipping costs and eliminating corrosion issues. Second, it utilizes polypropylene clips to connect vertical rebar to the horizontal stirrup, reducing onsite labor and eliminating human error. Thirdly, it features polypropylene fins on the outside to ensure the reinforcement is correctly positioned within the column form, a task typically accomplished with rebar wheels in the industry.

The formwork assembly includes a hoop reinforcement shaped to extend about the reinforcing bars. The hoop reinforcement is configured to provide shear strength to concrete poured into the formwork so positioned. The formwork assembly includes a plurality of receptacles circumferentially spaced-apart about, coupled to and radially inwardly-extending from the hoop reinforcement so as to promote a desired positioning or spacing of the reinforcing bars. The formwork assembly includes a plurality of spacers circumferentially spaced-apart about, coupled to and radially outwardly-extending from the hoop reinforcement. The formwork assembly includes a formwork shaped to extend about and be positioned in place via the plurality of spacers. data.title: Japan weighs tighter oversight of DeFi, self-custodial wallets
data.description:
Japan’s Financial Services Agency (FSA) is weighing potential new regulations for decentralized finance (DeFi) and self-custodial wallet providers as part of a broader effort to address risks associated with onchain finance.

In a discussion paper dated Thursday, the regulator raised the possibility of discouraging users from accessing DeFi services that lack adequate Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing controls.

The FSA also asked whether regulated businesses that interact with DeFi, including stablecoin issuers, on- and off-ramp providers and financial institutions, should play a role in mitigating illicit finance risks when no party responsible for regulatory compliance can be identified.

The regulator questioned how to identify parties responsible for DeFi services that claim to be decentralized but retain centralized elements, and whether front-end providers that give users access to decentralized exchanges should be subject to financial regulation.

The question of who should be held responsible for DeFi activities remains unresolved in other major markets. The European Union excludes fully decentralized crypto services without intermediaries from its Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation, while US regulators have largely focused on the nature of financial activities and the degree of control exercised by developers or operators. The stalled US CLARITY Act seeks to clarify which DeFi participants should be subject to financial regulation.

Japan weighs safeguards for self-custodial wallets

The FSA noted that direct regulation of self-custodial wallet use and providers that solely develop or sell software or hardware remains uncommon internationally but raised questions about whether additional measures are needed to protect users and prevent illicit financial activity.

Japan already requires domestic virtual asset service providers to collect information and maintain records on transactions involving self-custodial wallets, according to the FSA. Potential anti-fraud measures also include cooling-off periods for transfers from newly opened crypto exchange accounts to self-custodial wallets.

The discussions form part of a broader financial strategy announced by the FSA in July to promote onchain finance, with the initiative’s interim findings targeted for early 2027.

Further instructions can be found in the postal voting form.

  • Opening of the meeting
  • Election of chairman of the meeting
  • Preparation and approval of voting register
  • Presentation and approval of the agenda
  • Election of one or two persons to verify the minutes together with the chairman
  • Determination of whether the meeting has been duly convened
  • Resolution on a voluntary redemption program comprising (a) reduction of the share capital by way of redemption of shares for repayment to the shareholders and (b) increase of the share capital by way of bonus issue
  • Resolutions on (a) reduction of the share capital by way of cancellation of own shares and (b) increase of the share capital by way of bonus issue
  • Resolution to authorize the board of directors to undertake minor adjustments of the resolutions
  • Closure of the meeting

The board's proposals for resolutions

Item 2 – Election of chairman of the meeting

The board of directors proposes that the Chairman of the Board, Petter Nylander, is appointed as chairman of the meeting.

Item 3 – Preparation and approval of the voting register

The proposed voting register is the voting register that will have been prepared based on the shareholders present, the share register of the general meeting, and the postal votes received and that has been checked and approved by the persons elected to verify the minutes.

Item 7 – Resolution on a voluntary redemption program

Background and rationale

The purpose of the proposed redemption program is to reduce the number of shares in the Company and to return capital that is not deemed necessary for the business to the shareholders. The Company's repurchases of own shares are currently limited by the low liquidity of the share, which has meant that the Company has not been able to utilize its authorization to acquire own shares to the desired extent. A voluntary redemption program makes it possible to acquire and cancel a larger number of shares in a single structured transaction, on equal terms for all shareholders. The program gives each shareholder the opportunity to choose whether to have shares redeemed or to retain their shareholding.

Through the cost savings implemented during 2026, the group is profitable and the Company has a strong financial position without interest-bearing liabilities other than lease liabilities. The group has reduced the number of its own new games under development, and user acquisition to scale up a successful new game is deemed to be possible to finance with remaining funds and cash flow from operations. Furthermore, the distribution of third-party games on the G5 Store is a less capital-intensive business. The board of directors considers that the Company, also after the redemption program, will have a good equity ratio and satisfactory liquidity. For the board's assessment of the justifiability of the repayment, reference is made to the board's statement pursuant to Chapter 20, Section 8 of the Swedish Companies Act.

The board of directors proposes that the general meeting resolves on a voluntary redemption program of a total of not more than SEK 84,311,360 in accordance with items 7 (a) and 7 (b) below. The resolutions are conditional upon each other and are proposed to be adopted as one joint resolution.

An information brochure describing the voluntary redemption program in more detail will be published before trading in redemption rights and the application period commence.

Item 7 (a) – Reduction of the share capital by way of redemption of shares for repayment to the shareholders

The board of directors proposes that the general meeting resolves that the Company's share capital shall be reduced by not more than SEK 122,269.21 for repayment to the shareholders. The reduction shall be effected through redemption of not more than 1,053,892 ordinary shares, each with a quota value of approximately SEK 0.116. The repayment to the shareholders shall amount to a total of not more than SEK 84,311,360.

The reduction shall be carried out through a voluntary redemption program. Each ordinary share in the Company entitles the holder to one (1) redemption right. All holders of redemption rights are entitled to an equal right to redeem ordinary shares. No redemption rights, and thus no right to redeem shares, are received for class C shares or for ordinary shares held by the Company.

The record date for receipt of redemption rights shall be January 4, 2027. Seven (7) redemption rights entitle the holder to redemption of one (1) ordinary share.

For each ordinary share redeemed, the Company shall pay SEK 80 (the "Redemption Amount"), of which approximately SEK 79.88 exceeds the quota value of the share. The Redemption Amount corresponds to a premium of approximately 10 percent compared to the volume weighted average share price of the Company's ordinary share on Nasdaq Stockholm during the ten trading days preceding the day of the board's resolution on the proposal, November 26, 2026.

The part of the Redemption Amount exceeding the quota value of the shares shall be taken from the Company's unrestricted equity.

Customary trading in redemption rights and redemption shares will be arranged on Nasdaq Stockholm. The application period runs from and including January 7, 2027 up to and including January 21, 2027. Shareholders who do not tender shares for redemption will retain their ordinary shares unchanged.

Payment of the Redemption Amount shall be made through Euroclear Sweden AB after trading in redemption rights and redemption shares, respectively, has ended and after both the reduction of the share capital under this item 7 (a) and the bonus issue under item 7 (b) have been registered with the Swedish Companies Registration Office.

The board of directors is authorized to move the record date and the application period if required for technical reasons, without otherwise changing the terms of the redemption program.

Following the reduction of the share capital, the Company's share capital will amount to not less than SEK 806,120.68, divided into a total of not less than 6,948,308 shares, of which not less than 6,776,108 ordinary shares and 172,200 class C shares.

The board's statement pursuant to Chapter 20, Section 13, fourth paragraph of the Swedish Companies Act

The resolution to reduce the share capital under this item 7 (a) may be effectuated without obtaining an authorization from the Swedish Companies Registration Office or, in disputed cases, a court of general jurisdiction, as the Company simultaneously effectuates a bonus issue, as set out under item 7 (b) below, with an amount corresponding to no less than the amount the share capital is being reduced with, as set out above. Combined, these measures entail that neither the Company's restricted equity nor its share capital is reduced.

According to the annual report for the financial year 2025, which was published on April 29, 2026 and adopted by the Annual General Meeting on June 15, 2026, the amount available pursuant to Chapter 17, Section 3, first paragraph of the Swedish Companies Act amounts to SEK 340,390,000. Thereafter, the Annual General Meeting resolved, in accordance with the board's proposal, on a dividend to the shareholders of SEK 2.00 per share, in total SEK 15,131,500, and that the remaining earnings, SEK 325,258,500, be carried forward. On June 16, 2026, the board of directors resolved to initiate repurchases of own ordinary shares based on the authorization from the Annual General Meeting on June 15, 2026. At that time, the Company held 650,000 own ordinary shares and 172,200 own class C shares. During July 2026, 250,000 shares were cancelled in accordance with the resolution of the Annual General Meeting, and as of July 31, 2026, the Company held 400,000 own ordinary shares and 172,200 own class C shares. Since the repurchases were initiated, the Company has repurchased 52,752 shares for SEK 3,341,430. No other resolution on value transfer has been made.

Item 7 (b) – Increase of the share capital by way of bonus issue

With the purpose of restoring the share capital after the proposed reduction of the share capital under item 7 (a) above, the board of directors proposes that the general meeting at the same time resolves to increase the share capital by way of a bonus issue of SEK 122,269.21. The bonus issue shall be carried out without the issuance of new shares by transferring the amount from unrestricted equity.

Following the bonus issue, the Company's share capital will amount to SEK 928,389.89, divided into a total of not less than 6,948,308 shares, of which not less than 6,776,108 ordinary shares and 172,200 class C shares.

The resolution shall be executed as soon as possible after registration of the resolution with the Swedish Companies Registration Office.

Common provisions for item 7

The board of directors proposes that the resolutions under items 7 (a) and 7 (b) shall be adopted as one joint resolution. The resolutions are conditional upon each other.

The board's reports and the auditor's statements pursuant to Chapter 12 and Chapter 20, respectively, of the Swedish Companies Act will be made available as set out under "Complete proposals etc" below.

Majority requirement

A valid resolution in accordance with the board's proposal requires that the resolution is supported by shareholders representing at least 2/3 of the votes cast and the shares represented at the general meeting.

Item 8 – Resolutions on (a) reduction of the share capital by way of cancellation of own shares and (b) increase of the share capital by way of bonus issue

Item 8 (a) – Reduction of the share capital by way of cancellation of own shares

The board of directors proposes that the general meeting resolves to reduce the share capital by SEK 34,805.05 by way of cancellation of 300,000 own ordinary shares held by the Company which have been repurchased based on authorizations given at previous general meetings. With the purpose of restoring the share capital, the board of directors proposes that the general meeting at the same time resolves to increase the share capital by way of a bonus issue of SEK 34,805.05, without the issuance of new shares, by transfer from unrestricted equity.

Following the implementation of the resolutions under items 8 (a) and 8 (b), the Company's share capital will amount to an unchanged SEK 928,389.89, while the number of shares will decrease by 300,000.

Item 9 – Resolution to authorize the board of directors to undertake minor adjustments of the resolutions
